openBlockers.title: ch13-return Origin approach never lands: a repeating ~38.4 s orbital loop
openBlockers.detail: Booting ?story=ch13-return&movie=1 the signed ladder correctly boards (anc.cg.hatch-boarded at 2541 ms) and commits lift (anc.cg.lift-committed at 4560 ms), then enters ch13:return:origin. The ship genuinely flies: 412 marker-distance samples over 420 s. It is NOT a stalled body. It is a closed loop: the approach descends to a minimum of 50-51 m from the Origin audit site and then resets to ~2550 m, repeating 10 times with a period of ~38.4 s. Measured minima at 41.1, 79.4, 117.7, 155.2, 193.5, 231.8, 269.2, 306.7, 344.2, 382.6 s (all 50-51 m); measured maxima at 78.4, 116.7, 154.1, 192.4, 230.8, 268.2, 305.5, 343.1, 381.5, 418.9 s (all 2515-2562 m). Flight mode alternates descent/flight (54 samples) and deep_space/flight (358 samples). story:ch13-origin-landed never fires in 420 s. No rescue, teleport or grant was used or counted.
openBlockers.stallPredicateNote: Deliberately NOT reported as a body stall. The commission requires distinguishing a stationary seated body during MOVING flight from real stagnation; the body is correctly seated at [9.75, 51.10, -8] the whole time while the SHIP moves 2500 m per cycle. The discriminator used is the marker's own distance readout, not the body pose.
openBlockers.reportingCorrection: My probe's own first-vs-last summary field flightDistanceTrend says 'CLOSING' (2730 m -> 51 m). That label is naive and must not be quoted: it compares only endpoints and hides the oscillation. The per-sample profile above is the accurate statement.
